questions.question_text: The event is 'it rains tomorrow'. Which of these is the complementary event?

options.why: A day without rain is not necessarily sunny; a cloudy day with no rain also belongs to the complement.
The complement is the same event not happening, not a similar event on a different day.
Heavy rain is part of the event 'it rains tomorrow', not part of its complement.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of an event is the event not happening.
The complementary event is 'it does not rain tomorrow'.

questions.question_text: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Which set of outcomes is the complement of the event 'rolling a $5$'?

options.why: This is the event itself; the complement contains every other outcome of the sample space.
This is the whole sample space; the complement must leave out the outcome $5$.
The complement contains every outcome that is not $5$, not just the outcome after it.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of rolling a $5$ is not rolling a $5$.
As a set of outcomes: $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$.

questions.question_text: One card is drawn from a standard deck of $52$ cards. Which of these is the complement of the event 'drawing a heart'?

options.text: Drawing a diamond, club or spade

options.why: This misses the diamonds, which are red but are still not hearts.
Spades are only one of the three suits that are not hearts.
The red cards include the hearts themselves, so this overlaps the event.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of drawing a heart is not drawing a heart.
That is drawing a diamond, club or spade.

questions.question_text: Which pair of events is complementary?

options.text: Getting out of bed; not getting out of bed
Walking home from school; riding a bike home from school
options.why: Other ways of getting home exist, so the pair does not cover all outcomes.

options.text: Rolling at least a $3$ on a die; rolling $3$ or less on a die
options.why: Both events include rolling a $3$, so they overlap; complementary events share no outcomes.

options.text: Winning a football match; losing a football match
options.why: A draw is also possible, so the pair does not cover all outcomes.

questions.solution_text:
Complementary events cover all outcomes with no overlap.
An event and the same event not happening always form such a pair, so 'getting out of bed' and 'not getting out of bed' are complementary.

questions.question_text: Which of these is the complement of the event 'being under $15$ years old'?

options.why: This leaves out people who are exactly $15$; they are not under $15$, so they must be in the complement.
This describes the event itself, not the event failing to happen.
This includes everyone under $15$, so it overlaps the event instead of excluding it.

questions.solution_text:
The complement is not being under $15$ years old.
Someone who is exactly $15$ is not under $15$, so the complement is being $15$ or older.

questions.question_text: A bag contains red, green and blue marbles. One marble is picked at random. Which of these is the complement of the event 'picking a red or blue marble'?

options.why: Blue marbles belong to the event itself, not to its complement.

options.text: Picking a red or green marble
options.why: Red marbles belong to the event itself; the complement contains only outcomes outside the event.

options.text: Picking a red, green or blue marble
options.why: This is the whole sample space; the complement must exclude the red and blue marbles in the event.

questions.solution_text:
The complement is picking a marble that is neither red nor blue.
Green is the only other colour, so that is picking a green marble.

questions.question_text: Which of these is the complement of the event 'being born in winter'?

options.text: Being born in spring, summer or autumn

options.why: Summer is only one of the three seasons that are not winter.

options.text: Being born in autumn or spring
options.why: This leaves out summer, which is also not winter.

options.text: Being born in winter or summer
options.why: This includes the event itself, so it cannot be the complement.

questions.solution_text:
The complement is not being born in winter.
That is being born in spring, summer or autumn.

questions.question_text: A fair six-sided die is rolled. Which of these is the complement of the event 'rolling an even number'?

options.why: The outcome $6$ is even, so this set overlaps the event and leaves out the odd outcome $5$.
This includes the even outcome $2$ and leaves out the odd outcomes $3$ and $5$.
The number $2$ is both prime and even, so this overlaps the event.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of rolling an even number is not rolling an even number.
Every outcome on the die is even or odd, so the complement is rolling an odd number.
